articles.title: France is devouring itself as school riots reveal a crisis far bigger than broken classrooms
articles.summary: Student protests in France over crumbling schools expose deep tensions as Jean-Luc Mélenchon's La France Insoumise allegedly exploits the growing unrest.
articles.body:
Student protests over crumbling schools despite billions in public spending are fueling a broader crisis in France, and experts warn that the country's mounting financial troubles, President Emmanuel Macron's weakened political center and radical movements are pushing the unrest far beyond its original educational grievances.

Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies' senior envoy for Europe, told Fox News Digital in an interview from Paris that what began in September with legitimate complaints about school conditions has increasingly been exploited by political forces seeking confrontation with the state.

"Overall, I'd say the anger is real, but the violence, I would say, is organized," she said, adding that destroying schools would do nothing to improve the education system.

Seventy-two percent of education expenditures went toward salaries, social contributions and pensions for teaching and non-teaching personnel, while just 8.5% went toward investment, including infrastructure and equipment. The figures cover the entire education system, not just high schools, according to France's Education Ministry's 2026 statistical overview.

Harvey Feigenbaum, a professor of political science and international affairs at George Washington University and an expert on French politics, told Fox News Digital that France's underlying problem is a government caught between expensive social commitments, sluggish economic growth and mounting pressure to cut spending.

"France is in deep debt. It wants to cut its expenses," Feigenbaum said, explaining that years of financial pressure and neglected school facilities have fueled frustration among students.

The scale of the financial predicament is striking. According to Eurostat , French public debt stood at 117.6% of GDP in the first quarter of 2026, the third-highest ratio in the European Union, behind Greece and Italy.

Reuters reported Oct. 8 that rising borrowing costs and investor concerns have severely limited the government's ability to resolve unrest through additional spending, a strategy employed during previous waves of French protests.

The financial squeeze has collided with an increasingly fragmented political system , creating opportunities for parties at both ends of the political spectrum to capitalize on public dissatisfaction.

For Feigenbaum, the long-term roots of the crisis lie in Macron's political legacy.

When Macron won the presidency in 2017, he promised to move beyond France's traditional left-right divide, combining policies from both sides into a new centrist political movement.

But Feigenbaum argues that the strategy produced an unintended consequence, weakening France's established moderate parties without creating a durable governing coalition to replace them.

"What he ended up doing was attracting the moderate voters from the parties of the moderate left and the parties from the moderate right, and essentially destroyed those parties," Feigenbaum said.

He argued that the collapse of the traditional political center helped create space for more ideologically polarized movements.

"Macron is a smart man, but he's a terrible politician," the professor added.

Macron's controversial pension reforms illustrate the difficulty of persuading French voters to accept reductions in longstanding public benefits, Feigenbaum argued. Those efforts triggered widespread protests, while implementation of the 2023 retirement changes has since been suspended until 2028.

The situation became especially difficult after Macron called snap parliamentary elections in 2024, producing a deeply divided National Assembly without a governing majority.

"Even if the government wanted to do something coherent, they simply don't have the votes to do it," Feigenbaum said.

That paralysis has left Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu handling the immediate unrest while Macron faces questions about the stability of the political system he helped reshape.

The protests began in the Paris suburbs in September amid complaints about overcrowded classrooms , inadequate heating and cooling, aging buildings and teachers who were not replaced when absent.

Rodan-Benzaquen said the anger reflected years of educational instability, frequent ministerial changes and reforms that have failed to resolve persistent school problems.

She also pointed to a broader sense of anxiety among young people about their economic future, artificial intelligence, climate change and international conflicts.

According to the OECD's September 2026 Education at a Glance report , France spent $16,674 in funding per student in general upper secondary education in 2023, compared with an OECD average of $12,421, adjusted for purchasing power.

Yet teachers and students continue to complain about basic shortages.

Responsibility for public high school buildings and equipment falls to regional authorities, while the national government oversees much of the education system, including teacher staffing.

Feigenbaum said France's centralized education structure makes national leaders the focus of public anger when schools fail to deliver.

The pressure has already forced a concession.

Reuters reported Friday that Education Minister Édouard Geffray announced an emergency plan to deploy 3,000 qualified educators to particularly affected schools, costing several dozen million euros.

Student unions welcomed the measure as an initial victory but pledged to continue demonstrating.

The spending figures raise broader questions about whether France's financial and political priorities have left sufficient resources for maintaining school infrastructure and meeting students' needs. They do not, however, establish that teachers' unions or other organized constituencies have improperly diverted funding.

As the demonstrations expanded, the involvement of France's hard-left La France Insoumise party , known as LFI, led by Jean-Luc Mélenchon, became an increasingly contentious issue.

Reuters reported Oct. 1 that French intelligence agencies had told a government crisis meeting that LFI and affiliated activists played a role in fomenting the unrest. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez also cited agitators moving between schools to encourage violence.

LFI has denied responsibility and accused authorities of aggravating tensions through their response.

Rodan-Benzaquen said far-left movements were capitalizing on students' frustration.

"There is an obvious instrumentalization, obvious manipulation," she said, arguing that activists were seeking to push some protesters toward violence.

She linked the unrest to what she described as Mélenchon's broader political strategy ahead of France's 2027 presidential election.

"His idea is that, on the one hand, he will scare voters on the right and on the far right, who will then go to vote for the far right, and, on the other hand, he would mobilize his own camp," she said.

Rodan-Benzaquen argued that intensifying political confrontation could help Mélenchon consolidate his support among younger voters and immigrant communities, while portraying the far right as an increasingly serious threat.

She described it as a calculated political strategy rather than a spontaneous response to students' concerns.

The involvement of LFI politicians has been documented by French media, although there is disagreement over whether the party helped initiate the demonstrations or became involved after the protests began.

An Oct. 2 investigation by Le Monde examined a police intelligence assessment describing radical left activity around schools in Seine-Saint-Denis but questioned whether the evidence established that the movement itself was politically orchestrated.

Feigenbaum offered a more cautious interpretation, describing some of the violent perpetrators as fringe provocateurs who exploit broader demonstrations without necessarily directing them.

"They're not being organized by some, you know, some mastermind at the national level, at least as far as anyone knows," he said.

The demonstrations have also raised questions about whether Islamist groups and pro-Palestinian activists are seeking to use the unrest to advance broader ideological causes.

Rodan-Benzaquen argued that Mélenchon's emphasis on Gaza and the Palestinian cause has helped bring together political constituencies that might otherwise have little in common.

"It's sort of the idea of sort of an intersection of different movements where they manage to bring together the different groups, the far left, Islamist movements, pro-Palestinian activists," she said.

She pointed to Palestinian flags appearing during the demonstrations as an indication of how the movement has expanded beyond its original educational demands.

The FDD expert argued that Islamist elements were attempting to capitalize on the turmoil, although she cautioned against reducing the entire crisis to immigration or religion.

"But this goes far beyond the issue of immigration. It goes far beyond the issue of Islamism. It goes far beyond the issue of Islam," she said.

The government's latest concessions have not ended the protests.

According to Reuters on Friday , 141 schools remained closed while students continued demanding broader reforms. Nearly 10% of teaching hours in French public high schools remained unstaffed.

For Rodan-Benzaquen, one of the greatest dangers is that the demonstrations reflect a society increasingly divided into competing political realities.

She described how her 17-year-old son created separate left-wing and right-wing Instagram accounts and encountered radically different portrayals of the same unrest, one emphasizing police violence and the other violence by protesters.

"Now, if you live in two drastically different realities, it is very complicated to come to any form of dialog and end agreement," she said.

Her warning extends beyond France's current protests.

"We are in an extremely polarized environment," Rodan-Benzaquen said, noting that social media can deepen divisions and allow confrontations to escalate rapidly.

Feigenbaum sees an additional structural danger of a government burdened by accumulated financial obligations and deprived of the political consensus needed to reform them.

The result is a country spending heavily to sustain its public institutions while struggling to deliver the services citizens expect and a political system increasingly consumed by conflict over how to fix them.

What began as a rebellion against broken classrooms has become a test of whether France can reconcile its costly promises with its financial reality before the divisions consuming its schools deepen further.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed says Democrats must ‘win by massive numbers’ to fend off GOP election denial
articles.summary: Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee said he’s concerned that Trump and GOP candidate Mike Rogers “are not committed to the institution of our democracy.”
articles.body:
Michigan's Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed said his fellow Democrats need to "win by massive numbers" in the upcoming midterm elections so the result "is unquestionable."

"Donald Trump has already threatened to do what he did in 2020, which is deny the outcomes of an election," El-Sayed told NBC News' "Meet the Press" in an interview that aired Sunday.

Asked by NBC News on Saturday whether he would accept the results of the midterm elections no matter who wins, Trump said, "Of course I will. But we don't want cheating."

El-Sayed's Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, has also denied 2020 election results, El-Sayed told moderator Kristen Welker. "The guy I'm running against, he insinuates that he didn't actually lose in 2020," he said. "He talks about this mythical van that showed up in Detroit with a bunch of votes, as if he didn't lose."

Asked by Welker about whether he thinks Trump and Rogers would call his race into question if the results are close, El-Sayed said, "I am concerned that Donald Trump and Mike Rogers are not committed to the institution of our democracy."

After Joe Biden won the 2020 presidential election, Trump targeted Michigan with election fraud claims that were eventually shot down by a judge, who called them " nothing but speculation and conjecture ."

Michigan was also among a handful of states where Trump supporters in 2020 sought to submit a slate of so-called fake electors to the Electoral College to falsely declare that Trump won. Fifteen people were charged in the alleged scheme, but their cases were later dismissed .

Earlier this year, in a series of escalating inquiries about the state's voter rolls, the Trump administration demanded that Wayne County , home to Detroit, give the federal government all of its ballots from the 2024 presidential election.

In the "Meet the Press" interview, which was taped Friday, El-Sayed said he's confident he can win over former Trump voters with his campaign's economic focus. That includes making healthcare more accessible through "Medicare for All" and fighting corporate interests.

"Everywhere I go, I get somebody who comes up and says, 'Look, I voted for Trump two, three times, and I'm voting for you.' And I ask why. They say, 'It's because you really want me to have healthcare.' I really want them to have healthcare. 'It's because you really are America first.' I really am America first," said El-Sayed, a former public health official.

He also hopes those economic messages resonate with Jewish voters who may otherwise be skeptical of him because of his criticism of Israel and his rhetoric.

"The things that unite us are so much bigger than the things that divide us, so much bigger. We believe in religious pluralism. We believe in the separation of church and state. We believe that more people deserve healthcare. We believe in reproductive rights. We believe that Donald Trump is an existential threat on our democracy. We believe that corporations shouldn't be able to buy politicians," he said.

El-Sayed again expressed regret about his initial reaction to a March vehicle-ramming attack on a synagogue near Detroit. He condemned the attack at the time but added that " hurt people hurt people ," noting that some of the attacker's family members had died days earlier in airstrikes in Lebanon.

"If I step on somebody's grief, of course I regret that. And I really wish I'd thought about how somebody would have felt hearing that and thought twice about making those comments," El-Sayed told Welker.

"My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to my own kids," he added. "And we need to be able to know that we can go to our schools, that we can go to our places of worship, and that nobody is going to attack."

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which supports pro-Israel candidates from both parties, targeted El-Sayed's initial comments on the attack in mailers sent to voters this week.

A super PAC called Together for Michigan also began airing ads this week centered on the remarks. In one ad , a woman says her son was in the synagogue on the day of the attack, telling viewers that El-Sayed "gave an excuse to someone who wanted to murder children. I'm a lifelong Democrat, but this election, I'm voting for Mike Rogers."

With the final push to the midterms underway, Welker asked El-Sayed about his plans to campaign with former President Barack Obama. In a 2012 HuffPost opinion piece , El-Sayed wrote that "Obama was not the right choice. He just wasn't the wrong one. This leader has perpetrated war, violated our civil liberties, deported more people from our shores than any other president before him, and the list of his failures goes on."

On Friday, El-Sayed said that time has changed his perspective on Obama.

"I think about eight years of President Obama's leadership and you compare that to the 12 years we've lived since. You look back and say, 'Man, that was a really capable leader, who led with a kind of belief in people and uncommon grace, even for people who disagreed with him,'" El-Sayed said.

He added that he considers Obama a "mentor" and that great mentors "let you grow up."

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: Programa eleitoral vai ao ar sem áudio no dia 12 | G1
articles.standfirst: Propaganda eleitoral foi exibida às 13h, nesta segunda-feira (12), dia da padroeira do Brasil.
articles.summary: Exibida sem áudio, a propaganda eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro homenageou a padroeira do Brasil, tema também abordado no programa do candidato Lula nesta segunda-feira.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Afonso Ferreira/TV Globo e Divulgação/Ricardo Stuckert

O programa eleitoral do candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) foi ao ar sem áudio nesta segunda-feira (12). A campanha informou que ainda apura o que aconteceu. Flávio publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais em que criticou a exibição sem som.

A peça foi aberta com uma homenagem a Nossa Senhora Aparecida, padroeira do Brasil, cuja data é celebrada nesta segunda. O programa também contou com a participação do escritor Augusto Cury, que disputou a Presidência e foi derrotado no primeiro turno.

Na abertura, a peça fez referência à data como um momento para o Brasil lembrar de sua padroeira e reconhecer a fé de seu povo.

O TSE confirmou em nota que a exibição da propaganda eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro foi ao ar sem áudio por um erro técnico. Segundo a Corte Eleitoral, o programa irá ao ar em outro momento, ainda não definido. "O arquivo com a propaganda do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro foi corrigido e será reexibido", diz o tribunal, em nota.

A Associação Brasileira de Televisões e Rádios Legislativas (Astral) e a Associação Brasileira de Emissoras de Rádio e Televisão (Abert) informaram que receberam da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro o material em perfeitas condições. O problema ocorreu no processamento da mídia e foi prontamente comunicada ao TSE (leia a íntegra da nota no final desta reportagem).

Na última semana da campanha para o 1º turno das eleições de 2026, Nossa Senhora Aparecida foi alçada ao centro do debate político nacional. A circulação de publicações que atribuíram a Flávio a intenção de retirar da Santa o título de Padroeira do Brasil, informação negada pelo candidato, provocou reações de adversários, da Conferência Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB) e da Justiça .

Já o programa do presidente Lula (PT), candidato à reeleição, concentrou-se no custo de vida e em medidas para ampliar o poder de compra das famílias. A peça também mencionou o Dia das Crianças e o Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

A propaganda associou Flávio ao governo de Jair Bolsonaro e criticou a gestão do ex-presidente na economia. A campanha petista afirmou que, naquele período, os preços dos alimentos dispararam e a fome voltou a crescer no país.

Em sua participação, Lula reconheceu que o custo de vida continua elevado e disse que trabalha para reduzir os preços.

Leia abaixo a nota da Associação Brasileira de Televisões e Rádios Legislativas (Astral) e da Associação Brasileira de Emissoras de Rádio e Televisão (Abert):

"Em atenção às falhas de áudio registradas na propaganda eleitoral desta segundafeira (12), a ASTRAL (Associação Brasileira de Televisões e Rádios Legislativas) e a ABERT (Associação Brasileira de Emissoras de Rádio e Televisão) informam que a equipe técnica do “grupo único” de emissoras públicas e privadas, constituído em conjunto com o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) para a transmissão da propaganda eleitoral gratuita, identificou um problema técnico no processamento da mídia da campanha do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro, originalmente recebida do partido político em perfeitas condições. A ocorrência foi comunicada prontamente ao TSE.

A operação do grupo único para a transmissão da propaganda eleitoral, modelo consolidado ao longo de diversas eleições, é realizada de forma compartilhada pelas emissoras participantes que disponibilizam profissionais e equipamentos para o recebimento, preparação, geração e distribuição do sinal da propaganda eleitoral.

Considerando que a representação do candidato já apresentou petição à Justiça Eleitoral, as emissoras aguardam o posicionamento do TSE, conforme os procedimentos previstos na legislação eleitoral para situações dessa natureza".

articles.title: Flávio comemora liberação para visitas a Jair Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta segunda, Moraes autorizou a retomada de visitas de Flávio a Jair Bolsonaro, mas vetou a divulgação de manifestações do ex-presidente com finalidade político-eleitoral.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro visita Jair Bolsonaro nesta terça-feira após o ministro Alexandre de Moraes autorizar a retomada dos encontros, proibindo manifestações políticas.
articles.body:
O candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro , celebrou nesta segunda-feira (12) a decisão do ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), que libera visitas do senador ao pai , o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro .

Ele afirmou que, pelas regras definidas pela Justiça, não será possível visitar o pai nesta segunda por ser feriado, mas que nesta terça irá ao encontro do ex-presidente, que está preso em regime domiciliar por tentativa de golpe .

"Fiquei muito feliz que, no dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, é o dia que eu estou novamente autorizado a visitar o meu pai, vítima de uma injustiça. Hoje é só pra agradecer a Deus, agradecer a todo mundo que tá orando que tá rezando pelo nosso Brasil", declarou Flávio.

Condenado a 27 anos e 3 meses de prisão, Jair Bolsonaro cumpre a pena na sua casa, no Jardim Botânico, em Brasília.

"Estou ansioso, são mais de três meses sem poder vê-lo por uma decisão, obviamente, sem critério nenhum, nenhum amparo legal", completou o candidato do PL, criticando a restrição que havia sido imposta pelo ministro do STF.

Mais cedo, nesta segunda, Moraes atendeu a um pedido da defesa do ex-presidente e autorizou a retomada de visitas de Flávio a Jair Bolsonaro , mas vetou a divulgação de manifestações do ex-presidente com finalidade político-eleitoral .

Nossa Senhora no centro do debate político

Flávio comentou a decisão de Moraes durante declaração à imprensa após participar de uma missa em homenagem à Nossa Senhora Aparecida, na Catedral de Brasília.

Ele estava acompanhado do candidato a vice, Alfredo Gaspar (PL); da esposa, Fernanda; da coordenadora da campanha na área econômica, Daniella Marques; e de parlamentares aliados, como o deputado eleito Izalci Lucas (PL-DF) e a senadora eleita Bia Kicis (PL-DF).

Na última semana da campanha para o 1º turno das eleições de 2026, Nossa Senhora Aparecida foi alçada ao centro do debate político nacional.

A circulação de publicações que atribuíram a Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) a intenção de retirar da Santa o título de Padroeira do Brasil – informação negada pelo candidato – provocou reações de adversários, da Conferência Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB) e foi parar na Justiça.

🔎A polêmica sobre a padroeira do Brasil começou após postagens associarem a Flávio Bolsonaro um projeto para tirar da Santa o título de Padroeira do Brasil.

🔎Apoiadores de Lula ( PT ) passaram a explorar os posts politicamente e a disputa foi levada ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), que liberou publicações na web sobre o tema, desde que não associem o projeto ao candidato do PL.

articles.title: Lula promete concluir meta de 3 milhões de moradias pelo Minha Casa, Minha Vida | G1
articles.standfirst: Após missa por Nossa Senhora Aparecida no Palácio da Alvorada, presidente também defendeu o respeito à liberdade religiosa e falou sobre segurança pública e escala 6x1.
articles.summary: Após missa por Nossa Senhora Aparecida no Palácio da Alvorada, presidente também defendeu o respeito à liberdade religiosa e falou sobre segurança pública e escala 6x1.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, candidato à reeleição pelo PT, participou de uma missa em homenagem a Nossa Senhora Aparecida na capela do Palácio da Alvorada, em Brasília.

Lula esteve acompanhado da primeira-dama, Janja da Silva, de ministros, além de famílias e crianças ligadas a movimentos sociais. A celebração também fez referência ao Dia das Crianças.

Na saída da cerimônia, o presidente defendeu a liberdade religiosa .

"Num país civilizado, um país harmônico, um país democrático, ou seja, cada um segue a religião que quiser, e todos nós temos que respeitar. Ninguém é obrigado a ser da mesma religião. O que nós precisamos apenas é respeitar a fé e a espiritualidade das pessoas como elas são. Tenho em Nossa Senhora Aparecida uma referência da minha espiritualidade e da minha fé. Esse gesto foi muito importante para mim e é muito importante para o povo católico brasileiro", afirmou.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) participou de uma missa em homenagem a Nossa Senhora Aparecida — Foto: Globo/ Reprodução

Ainda durante a entrevista concedida no Palácio da Alvorada, Lula falou sobre o programa Minha Casa, Minha Vida e afirmou que, se reeleito, pretende entregar 3 milhões de moradias contratadas até o fim deste ano .

O presidente também defendeu a aprovação do projeto que prevê o fim da escala de trabalho 6 por 1. A votação da proposta está prevista para quarta-feira (14) no plenário do Senado.

Lula afirmou ainda que pretende criar o Ministério da Segurança Pública caso o Senado aprove a PEC da Segurança, que estabelece a coordenação de ações entre o governo federal e os estados no combate ao crime organizado.

"Na medida em que o governo federal assumir o papel da segurança pública, na medida em que a Constituição permitir, a gente vai poder dizer alto e bom som que, para o povo trabalhador, a gente quer tranquilidade, a gente quer paz, a gente quer proteção. Para o território, a gente quer paz, a gente quer proteção. Agora, para os bandidos, a gente quer prisão".

No Rio de Janeiro, movimentos estudantis organizaram uma manifestação em apoio a Lula, sem a presença do candidato, em Copacabana.

No início da tarde, apoiadores ocuparam sete quarteirões da Avenida Atlântica.

No fim do dia, uma outra manifestação, organizada por sambistas, reuniu apoiadores do presidente na Lapa, na região central da capital fluminense.

articles.title: TSE manda Flávio Bolsonaro apagar vídeo enganoso sobre ato pró-Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo de mulher com suposta substância ilícita circulava em redes sociais antes de ato em São Paulo; ministro da Corte Eleitoral vê "grave manipulação"
articles.summary: O TSE determinou que Flávio Bolsonaro remova vídeo enganoso que associava uso de drogas à manifestação pró-Lula. Ministro Belizze citou grave manipulação de fatos.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro durante evento em São Paulo neste domingo (11) — Foto: Jean Carniel/Reuters

O ministro Marco Aurélio Belizze, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), determinou que Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) apague vídeo enganoso sobre a manifestação de apoiadores do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na Avenida Paulista no domingo (11) . Conteúdo publicado pelo candidato do PL usa imagens que não foram feitas no ato para sugerir uso de drogas por petistas.

"Essa forma de apresentação falsa e manipulada dos fatos, mesclando acontecimentos reais e situações que de fato não ocorreram é extremamente deletéria e pode caracterizar, como no caso dos autos, grave manipulação por descontextualização", diz Belizze em sua decisão.

As imagens mostram uma jovem de cabelo vermelho com outras duas pessoas ao seu redor, todos sentados no chão em um espaço que parece ser aberto. Na gravação, ela inala um pó branco que se assemelha a cocaína. Como já mostrou o Fato ou Fake, o vídeo já circulava na internet antes de a manifestação a favor de Lula ser realizada.

Uma conta no X baseada na Argentina publicou o vídeo em 10 de outubro, na véspera do ato na Paulista. Uma conta chilena no X, de uma usuária que se diz "nacionalista" e "anticomunista", também compartilhou o vídeo. Sua postagem associa a jovem do vídeo a um protesto realizado no país a favor da Palestina.

Segundo os documentos da ação no TSE, o vídeo teria sido publicado originalmente no Chile.

O ministro deu 24 horas para que Flávio e o senador eleito Carlos Bolsonaro (PL-SC), além do empresário Pablo Marçal (PRTB) e do deputado federal eleito Rony Gabriel (Podemos-RS), apagarem as publicações nas quais usaram imagens da jovem. Também determina que a Meta tire do ar publicação similar feita pelo perfil Sociedade em Fatos, além de identificar o responsável pela página.

Belizze diz ainda em sua decisão que críticas ao ato podem ser feitas por grupos políticos, mas não com o uso de manipulação e descontextualização sobre os fatos. "A medida não impede críticas, opiniões ou publicações sobre a manifestação que não apresentem o vídeo anteriormente mencionado como registro do evento."

articles.title: Gilmar Mendes lamenta derrota de Esperidião Amin ao Senado por SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro do STF usou rede social para exaltar senador: 'Marcou a política catarinense'. Amin ficou em terceiro lugar na disputa e ficará fora de cargos eletivos após 17 anos.
articles.summary: Amin ficou em terceiro lugar na disputa e ficará fora de cargos eletivos após 17 anos.
articles.body:
Gilmar Mendes e Esperidião Amin — Foto: Rosinei Coutinho/SCO/STF - Luis Macedo/Câmara dos Deputados

O ministro Gilmar Mendes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), usou as redes sociais para lamentar a derrota do senador Esperidião Amin ( PP ), que não foi reeleito para o cargo em Santa Catarina .

Em uma publicação de sábado (10) na rede social X (ex-Twitter), o magistrado citou uma frase do ex-presidente do Senado Jarbas Passarinho após a derrota de Djalma Marinho na eleição de 1974, refletindo que "os movimentos populares têm sua lógica e sua irracionalidade".

Disse ainda que "poucos nomes marcaram tanto a política catarinense" como Amin, hoje com 78 anos. Frisou a longa trajetória do senador, que foi governador do estado, prefeito de Florianópolis e deputado federal.

"Santa Catarina e o Congresso Nacional deixarão, lamentavelmente, de contar, a partir de 2027, com a experiência e o talento político de Amin. Permanece, porém, todo o legado de uma atuação séria e comprometida com o melhor interesse público. Estou certo de que ele continuará a desempenhar um papel fundamental para os catarinenses e para o país", escreveu Gilmar Mendes.

Com o revés, Amin ficará de fora de cargos eletivos a partir de 2027, o que não acontecia há 16 anos. Ele ficou em terceiro lugar na disputa para o Senado nas eleições de 4 de outubro.

O político recebeu 1.233.034 votos, representando 15,31% dos válidos. As duas vagas a partir de 2027 serão de Carol De Toni e Carlos Bolsonaro, ambos do PL, e estreantes no cargo.

Confira a postagem completa de Gilmar Mendes:

Diante da derrota de Djalma Marinho na eleição para senador, em 1974, Jarbas Passarinho observou que os movimentos populares têm sua lógica e sua irracionalidade. Essa reflexão ecoa agora, com a não reeleição de Esperidião Amin para o Senado Federal.

Poucos nomes marcaram tanto a política catarinense. Foram quase seis décadas de vida pública. Prefeito de Florianópolis por duas vezes, assumiu o governo do Estado aos 35 anos. Em 1998, foi eleito novamente governador. Foi eleito deputado federal três vezes e senador da República duas vezes, presidiu nacionalmente seu partido e disputou a Presidência em 1994. No Senado, teve atuação constante em favor do desenvolvimento regional e da infraestrutura do Estado, além de iniciativas de apoio ao crédito para micro e pequenos empreendedores, entre tantas outras causas meritórias.

Santa Catarina e o Congresso Nacional deixarão, lamentavelmente, de contar, a partir de 2027, com a experiência e o talento político de Amin. Permanece, porém, todo o legado de uma atuação séria e comprometida com o melhor interesse público. Estou certo de que ele continuará a desempenhar um papel fundamental para os catarinenses e para o país.

articles.title: 'Gostaria de ser a primeira mulher presidente do Senado', diz Tereza Cristina | G1
articles.standfirst: Senadora do PP também disse disse que pretende apresentar emendas 'para melhorar' a PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1.
articles.summary: Senadora do PP também disse disse que pretende apresentar emendas 'para melhorar' a PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1.
articles.body:
A senadora Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) afirmou nesta segunda-feira (12) que gostaria de ser a primeira mulher a presidir o Senado Federal. Ela disse que já conversou com o atual presidente da Casa, Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), e com outros senadores sobre a possibilidade.

Em entrevista ao Estúdio i, Tereza Cristina afirmou que está na metade de seu mandato de oito anos e que ainda não sabe se disputará uma nova eleição. Por isso, gostaria de deixar um legado, especialmente para as mulheres.

“Eu sempre disse que gostaria de ser a primeira mulher presidente do Senado, mesmo porque eu tenho comigo que esse talvez seja o meu único mandato no Senado, eu não sei se eu quero disputar outro, e eu gostaria de deixar um legado, principalmente para as mulheres”, afirmou.

Ela disse que tem conversado com colegas sobre a sucessão, mas ressaltou que a escolha dependerá da composição da Casa a partir de 2027.

Questionada se disputaria o cargo contra Alcolumbre, Tereza Cristina afirmou que essa possibilidade não foi descartada.

“Isso nunca foi colocado, eu sempre disse a ele que eu gostaria de ser a sua sucessora, a sua sucessora pode ser agora ou pode ser depois, então a gente tem que ver como é que as coisas vão se encaminhar”, disse.

A parlamentar também citou o senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), que tem interesse em disputar a presidência do Senado, e disse ter maior alinhamento político com ele.

“É claro que eu, sendo uma senadora de centro-direita, eu vou estar muito mais alinhada com o Rogério Marinho, que também tem essa pretensão”, afirmou.

Segundo Tereza Cristina, as articulações para a escolha do próximo presidente do Senado também dependerão do resultado do segundo turno presidencial.

Tereza Cristina também comentou sobre a proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, cuja votação está prevista para quarta-feira (14).

A senadora afirmou que pretende discutir com a oposição a apresentação de emendas para alterar o texto. Ela considera que a proposta precisa de mais debate sobre os possíveis impactos na economia e no emprego.

“Mas vai ser colocada para votar, eu acho que talvez a pressa seja eleitoreira, nós precisaríamos ter mais tempo para essa discussão, mas tudo indica que será colocado na quarta-feira, e aí nós vamos ter que votar, vamos votar, e tentar talvez algumas emendas para tentar melhorar a PEC, porque eu acho que ela pode ser melhorada”, disse.

Para Tereza Cristina, o principal problema é incluir na Constituição regras sobre a escala de trabalho, diante das diferenças entre os setores da economia.

A senadora afirmou que a redução dos dias trabalhados precisa ser discutida com cuidado para evitar possíveis impactos sobre os preços e a disponibilidade de trabalhadores em determinadas atividades.

Ela ressaltou, porém, que não é contrária à ampliação do descanso semanal dos trabalhadores.

Tereza Cristina também afirmou que vê espaço no Senado, a partir de 2027, para discussões sobre pedidos de impeachment de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

Segundo ela, o tema esteve presente na campanha de candidatos ao Senado e deverá ser cobrado dos parlamentares eleitos.

“Eu vejo ambiente sim, vejo que foi uma pauta”, afirmou.

A senadora disse que a discussão sobre a atuação do Supremo não deve ser a única prioridade da próxima legislatura, mas avaliou que o tema ganhou importância nas eleições.

“Infelizmente, esse foi um tema que foi central nessas eleições e nós seremos cobrados, sim, por abrir para investigar o que está acontecendo, os fatos que estão aí postos sobre o Supremo Tribunal Federal”, disse.

articles.title: Defesa Civil alerta para chuva e ventos de 100 km/h | G1
articles.standfirst: Sorocaba (SP) teve alerta da Defesa Civil do Estado nesta segunda-feira (12). Persistência das instabilidades e saturação do solo aumentam o risco de alagamentos, enxurradas e transbordamentos de rios e córregos.
articles.summary: Chuvas fortes em SP e solo saturado aumentam o risco de alagamentos, quedas de árvores e transtornos em diversas regiões até quinta-feira (15).
articles.body:
Alerta vale também para Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A Defesa Civil alertou para a manutenção do tempo instável entre terça-feira (13) e quinta-feira (15), com previsão de chuva nas regiões de Sorocaba , Jundiaí , Bauru , Presidente Prudente e Itapetininga (SP).

Segundo o órgão, há previsão de pancadas de chuva em todo o estado, acompanhadas de raios e rajadas de vento. Não estão descartados temporais e queda pontual de granizo.

Na terça-feira, os acumulados poderão ser expressivos, sobretudo nas regiões oeste e sul do estado. Na quarta-feira (14), são esperadas chuvas generalizadas, de intensidade moderada a forte, com maiores acumulados nas regiões oeste, sul, centro e leste paulista.

Na quinta-feira, as pancadas de chuva persistem em todo o território paulista, com possibilidade de volumes expressivos principalmente nas regiões que fazem divisa com Minas Gerais.

Diante desse cenário, a Defesa Civil orienta a população a população a acompanhar os comunicados oficiais e adotar medidas preventivas durante os períodos de chuva intensa.

Um alerta severo foi emitido para a região de Sorocaba (SP) na noite desta segunda-feira (12). O informe indica a possibilidade de ocorrência de chuvas, raios, ventos e condição para granizo.

A Defesa Civil reforçou a importância de manter o celular habilitado para receber alertas de emergência.

Para receber avisos por SMS, basta enviar o CEP da localidade desejada para o número 40199 . Em situações de emergência, os telefones são 199 , da Defesa Civil, e 193 , do Corpo de Bombeiros.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) também publicou um aviso para chuvas e ventos fortes a partir da 0h de quarta-feira (14). O instituto prevê chuva entre 30 e 60 mm/h ou 50 e 100 mm/dia, e ventos intensos (60-100 km/h) . Além disso, há previsão de queda de granizo.

Com a situação, o alerta lembra do risco de corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de árvores e de alagamentos. A previsão é válida para as regiões de Sorocaba, Jundiaí e Itapetininga.

articles.title: Vestibular UEA 2026: 12,4 mil faltam no 1º dia; provas seguem hoje | G1
articles.standfirst: A seleção oferece 2.024 vagas em cursos de graduação, e os candidatos fazem nesta terça-feira (13) as provas de Conhecimentos Específicos e Redação.
articles.summary: O Vestibular UEA 2026 registrou 12,4 mil ausências no primeiro dia. Nesta terça (13), candidatos concorrem a 2.024 vagas em provas específicas e redação.
articles.body:
Expectativas de ingresso na universidade marcam primeiro dia do Vestibular da UEA em 2026 — Foto: Foto: Gustavo Rodrigues/UEA

A Universidade do Estado do Amazonas (UEA) registrou 12.415 ausências no primeiro dia do Vestibular 2026, acesso 2027, nesta segunda-feira (12). O número representa 34,92% dos candidatos inscritos. As provas de Conhecimentos Gerais foram aplicadas em 140 locais, sendo 41 em Manaus e 99 no interior do estado.

Ao todo, a UEA oferta 5.062 vagas em cursos de graduação por meio do Vestibular e do Sistema de Ingresso Seriado (SIS). Desse total, 2.024 vagas são destinadas ao Vestibular e 3.038 ao SIS. As duas seleções reúnem 84.575 candidatos inscritos, que concorrem a oportunidades de ingresso na instituição.

O processo seletivo continua nesta terça-feira (13/10), com as provas de Conhecimentos Específicos e Redação. O Vestibular conta com 35.553 inscritos.

Com diferentes trajetórias e expectativas para o futuro, estudantes deram mais um passo em direção ao ingresso na universidade, com oportunidades de formação pública de qualidade distribuídas na capital e no interior do estado.

No primeiro dia de aplicação das provas do Vestibular, foi registrada abstenção de 34,92% dos candidatos. Ao todo, 23.138 candidatos compareceram para a prova de Conhecimentos Gerais, nesta segunda-feira (12).

Candidato a uma vaga na UEA, Hiram Sebastião, de 18 anos, almeja ingressar no mais novo curso da universidade: Medicina Veterinária, em Presidente Figueiredo, lançado neste ano.

“A razão pela qual escolhi esse curso é porque Medicina Veterinária é uma área que sempre esteve presente na minha vida, desde mais novo, sempre criei animais em casa e fui muito fascinado e interessado por eles, tanto pela sua biologia e afins. Minhas expectativas são de fazer uma ótima prova, conseguir um bom resultado e, é claro, ser aprovado.”

Para Maria Clara Oliveira, de 18 anos, o Vestibular da UEA é uma grande oportunidade para ingressar no ensino superior no Amazonas.

“Eu sei que é um concurso extremamente concorrido. É uma grande oportunidade estar aqui, tanto agora quanto no próximo ano. Eu acredito muito que eu vou passar porque eu tenho bastante fé e as minhas expectativas são muito altas para prova de agora."

Entre as novidades desta edição está a ampliação das oportunidades de formação no interior do estado, com a oferta de Medicina Veterinária, no Núcleo de Ensino Superior de Presidente Figueiredo (Nespf); Farmácia, no Centro de Estudos Superiores de Tefé (Cest); Licenciatura em Computação, em Iranduba; e Letras - Língua Portuguesa e Matemática, voltado à comunidade indígena Belém do Solimões, em Tabatinga.

No domingo (11), a UEA aplicou as provas do SIS, que contou com 49.022 candidatos inscritos. A seleção ocorreu em 173 locais, sendo 77 em Manaus e 96 no interior do estado. O SIS é organizado em três etapas anuais e consecutivas, correspondentes às três séries do ensino médio.

O resultado final do Vestibular e do SIS tem divulgação prevista para 27 de novembro de 2026, mesma data estimada para a publicação do edital de matrícula.

articles.title: Nunes Marques proíbe jornal que compara Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: O ministro ordenou a interrupção da distribuição e circulação do jornal "por qualquer meio, físico ou digital" sob pena de multa de R$ 10 mil por ato. A decisão é preliminar e deverá ser analisada pelo plenário da corte.
articles.summary: Nunes Marques proibiu a circulação de jornal do Sindicato dos Petroleiros que comparava Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro, sob pena de multa diária de R$ 10 mil.
articles.body:
O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques decidiu, nesta segunda-feira (12), retirar de circulação um jornal produzido pelo Sindicato Unificado dos Petroleiros do Estado de São Paulo, Goiás e Distrito Federal, ligado a Federeção Única dos Petroleiros (FUP). A decisão é preliminar e deverá ser analisada pelo plenário da corte.

Em nota, a Federação Única dos Petroleiros (FUP) chamou a decisão de "censura" e um "grave ataque à liberdade de expressão".

“A medida representa um grave ataque à liberdade de expressão e ao direito de informar a população. É dever dos sindicatos fornecer informações fidedignas a seus filiados, a fim de que possam conhecer projetos, comparar propostas e decidir pelo melhor para o país e para os brasileiros”, afirmou Cibele Vieira, coordenadora-geral da FUP.

O ministro ordenou a interrupção da distribuição e circulação do jornal "por qualquer meio, fisico ou digital" sob pena de multa de R$ 10 mil por ato. Além disso, o presidente do TSE determinou o recolhimento dos exemplares que não foram distribuídos e a retirada do material do site do sindicato.

O pedido foi feito pela campanha do candidato à Presidência da República e senador, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), que justificou que o jornal é uma produção "de inequívoca finalidade político-eleitoral".

"Sob o título 'O FUTURO DO BRASIL ESTÁ EM SUAS MÃOS', o Sindicato dirige-se diretamente ao eleitor e contrapõe as duas candidaturas presidenciais, afirmando que o eleitor deverá escolher entre "dois projetos de Brasil radicalmente diferentes", justificou.

Nunes Marques reconheceu o pedido da campanha de Flávio apontando que "as liberdades públicas não são incondicionais e que nenhum direito individual pode converter-se em escudo para condutas ilícitas".

"É importante ressaltar, portanto, que a liberdade de expressão não constitui salvo-conduto para a prática de ilícitos eleitorais nem autoriza a quebra da paridade de armas que rege o processo eleitoral", finalizou.

Nunes Marques em sessão Plenária TSE 06.10.2026 — Foto: Leobark Rodrigues/Secom/TSE

O períodico, publicado em edição especial com uma tiragem de 30 mil unidades, foi analisada página a página pelo ministro Nunes Marques, que foi delimitando o conteúdo que entendia como propaganda-eleitoral.

Em determinado trecho, o jornal traz um quadro com fotografias de Adriano da Nóbrega, Rodrigo Bacellar, Daniel Vorcaro e Fabrício Queiroz associando as pessoas a Flávio Bolsonaro e afirma que "quem convive com chefe de milícia, aliado de facção e banqueiro investigado não pode ser levado a sério quando fala em ‘combater o crime organizado'".

Em resposta, Nunes Marques indica que o contraponto sobre Lula não é igual a de Bolsonaro.

"Em contraste, atribui ao 'governo Lula' o enfrentamento do crime organizado e encerra com indagação dirigida ao leitor sobre quem 'protege o povo', arrematando que 'a resposta está nos fatos, não no discurso de campanha'", apontou o ministro.

articles.title: Agentes federais dos EUA fazem buscas na casa de deputada democrata nascida na Somália | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação apura suposta fraude imigratória envolvendo documentos apresentados pelo pai de Ilhan Omar; operação ocorre a 22 dias das eleições legislativas, em que ela disputa o quinto mandato.
articles.summary: Investigação apura suposta fraude imigratória envolvendo documentos apresentados pelo pai de Ilhan Omar; operação ocorre a 22 dias das eleições legislativas, em que ela disputa o quinto mandato.
articles.body:
Agentes federais dos Estados Unidos fizeram buscas na casa de uma deputada do Partido Democrata, nascida na Somália. Os investigadores alegam que estão apurando uma suposta fraude na documentação preenchida pelo pai dela, quando a atual deputada ainda era criança.

Os agentes chegaram à casa da deputada federal Ilhan Omar, nos arredores da capital, Washington, antes do amanhecer. A operação ocorreu 22 dias antes da eleição pro Congresso em que a deputada do Partido Democrata concorreu a um quinto mandato.

O Departamento de Justiça Americano evita operações contra candidatos nos 60 dias que antecederam a votação, salvo discussões sobre risco de destruição de provas ou à segurança de pessoas. Os investigadores não revelaram o motivo da operação.

Segundo a imprensa americana, apuram uma suposta fraude imigratória e querem avaliar documentos preenchidos pelo pai de Omar quando ela era criança. Nascida na Somália, ela foi para os EUA com a família fugindo da guerra civil. Hoje é deputada por Minnesota, estado com a maior comunidade somali do país.

No mês passado, o secretário de Segurança Interna sugeriu que Ilhan Omar poderia ser deportada.

Numa rede social, a deputada escreveu: “Não se enganem: esta é uma tentativa de perseguir adversários políticos e transformar as forças federais de segurança em uma arma política”. O líder da minoria democrata na Câmara, Hakeem Jeffries, chamou a operação de abuso de poder.

Donald Trump já fez diversos ataques a Ilhan Omar. Em mais de uma ocasião, a chamou de lixo. No sábado, no Tennessee, Trump disse: "Tudo o que eles têm na Somália é crime e miséria".

O presidente tem viajado pelo país em comícios pedindo votos para o partido na eleição parlamentar do mês que vem. As pesquisas indicam que o Partido Republicano pode perder a maioria no Congresso em parte por causa da impopularidade registrada de Trump. O principal motivo é a inflação causada pela guerra contra o Irã.

Hoje, o jornal New York Times revelou que o trilionário Elon Musk se tornou o maior doador da história do país numa eleição de meio de mandato. Uma votação que vai renovar toda a Câmara e 1/3 do Senado. Desde julho, Musk já doou 276 milhões de dólares para o Partido Republicano -- o equivalente a R$ 1,4 bilhão. O que Musk doou é mais do que o partido Democrata, de oposição, arrecadou de todos os doadores neste mesmo período.

articles.title: Marijuana Is On The Ballot In 2026. The Debate Has Changed
articles.summary: Marijuana is on the ballot in Massachusetts, Idaho, and Houston in 2026. Explore the proposed changes and potential implications for employers.
articles.body:
Ten years after Massachusetts voters legalized recreational marijuana, they're being asked to reverse course. Meanwhile, voters in Idaho and Houston will weigh in on who gets to decide marijuana policy and how existing laws should be enforced.

The November 3 election offers an interesting snapshot of how the marijuana debate is changing. And for employers, the results could have implications for everything from workplace accommodations to drug testing and criminal background checks.

Massachusetts: Could Legalization Go Into Reverse?

Massachusetts voters approved recreational marijuana in 2016, and the industry has grown considerably since then. In September, the state's Cannabis Control Commission reported that recreational marijuana businesses had surpassed $10 billion in cumulative sales .

Now, voters are being asked whether to dismantle that market.

Question 8 would eliminate recreational marijuana sales, the associated tax and regulatory framework, and home cultivation. Adults 21 and older could still possess up to one ounce, subject to limits on concentrates, without penalties. Medical marijuana would remain legal.

If approved, the measure would take effect January 1, 2028. Massachusetts would become the first state to repeal a voter-approved recreational marijuana market.

So, why reconsider legalization after a decade?

Supporters point to concerns about youth access, impaired driving, mental health, and the commercialization of cannabis. They argue that the regulated market has brought consequences voters didn't fully anticipate in 2016.

Opponents warn that eliminating recreational sales could push consumers toward illicit markets, eliminate tax revenue, and threaten businesses and jobs.

It's a notable shift in a country where marijuana policy has generally moved toward greater legalization. Massachusetts could become a test of whether voters are willing to revisit an established cannabis market.

For businesses operating in that market, the stakes are substantial. Recreational retailers, cultivators, and other operators could face significant disruption, although qualifying businesses could seek medical marijuana licenses.

For other employers, the more immediate question is what happens to existing workplace protections.

Massachusetts legalized medical marijuana in 2012, and its courts have recognized that employees using marijuana to treat qualifying medical conditions may be entitled to reasonable accommodation.

In Barbuto v. Advantage Sales and Marketing , the state's highest court considered a case involving an employee who was terminated after testing positive for marijuana despite disclosing her medical use. The court concluded that the employer could have an obligation to consider a reasonable accommodation under state disability discrimination law, even though marijuana remained illegal federally.

Employers may still consider safety concerns, undue hardship, and applicable federal requirements. But they generally cannot dismiss an accommodation request simply because it involves medical marijuana.

Because Question 8 would preserve medical marijuana, those considerations would remain relevant regardless of the election outcome.

While Massachusetts voters reconsider a legalization decision made a decade ago, Idaho voters will decide who gets to make that decision in the future.

House Joint Resolution 4 would amend the state constitution to give the legislature exclusive authority to legalize marijuana, narcotics, and other psychoactive substances. Citizens could no longer use ballot initiatives to legalize those substances.

Idaho currently prohibits both recreational and medical marijuana. Advocates have repeatedly attempted to place medical marijuana legalization before voters, including an initiative that failed to qualify for the 2026 ballot.

Supporters of HJR 4 believe legalization decisions should go through the legislative process, where lawmakers can conduct hearings and evaluate proposed regulations. Opponents argue that the amendment would unnecessarily restrict voters' ability to change state law.

For employers, the immediate impact would be limited. Idaho's marijuana prohibitions and existing workplace drug-testing requirements would remain unchanged.

Under Idaho Code § 72-1705, employers seeking the protections of the state's Employer Alcohol and Drug-Free Workplace Act generally must maintain a written testing policy. The policy must identify the types of testing conducted, be communicated to affected employees and available to applicants, and explain that violations may result in termination for misconduct. The statute also recognizes an exception for qualifying collectively bargained policies.

Those requirements would remain in place regardless of the election outcome.

The longer-term significance is how Idaho's marijuana laws could evolve. In states where voters have approved legalization through ballot initiatives, those changes have sometimes prompted additional debates about drug testing, medical marijuana, and off-duty conduct.

Idaho voters will decide whether that path remains available.

Houston: Changing Enforcement Without Legalization

Houston voters will consider another approach to marijuana policy: making enforcement of certain marijuana offenses a lower priority for local police.

Proposition A would make enforcement of Class A and Class B misdemeanor marijuana possession the Houston Police Department's lowest law enforcement priority. It would also establish reporting requirements and prohibit no-knock search warrants by Houston police officers.

Marijuana possession would remain illegal under Texas law.

Texas does have a limited medical cannabis program. Its Compassionate Use Program allows qualifying patients to obtain prescribed low-THC cannabis for certain medical conditions. The state expanded that program in 2025, but Houston's proposal wouldn't change it.

For employers, the most relevant consideration may be criminal background screening.

If police make marijuana possession a lower enforcement priority, fewer arrests and prosecutions could follow. Over time, that could influence the marijuana-related records employers encounter when screening applicants.

But Proposition A wouldn't erase existing convictions or change the legal standards governing employment decisions based on criminal history.

Employers would still need to follow applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act when obtaining employment background reports from consumer reporting agencies.

Houston's proposal illustrates how marijuana policy can change at the local level, even when the underlying state criminal law remains the same.

Massachusetts could eliminate recreational sales while preserving medical marijuana accommodations. Idaho could restrict future citizen-led legalization efforts without changing its drug-testing laws. Houston could reduce enforcement priorities without legalizing marijuana.

Medical marijuana protections may continue even when recreational laws change. A positive drug test may indicate prior exposure without necessarily establishing current impairment. And changes in criminal enforcement may influence background screening without changing the laws governing employment decisions.

Federal requirements also remain important, particularly for employees in safety-sensitive positions subject to Department of Transportation drug-testing rules.

As results come in, employers should focus on what changes, when those changes take effect, and whether existing workplace policies need attention.

Voters will decide what direction marijuana policy takes next. Employers will have to navigate what those decisions mean in the workplace .

articles.title: The Latest: Rep. Omar says she will ‘not be silenced’ after Homeland Security searches her home
articles.summary: Federal agents on Monday searched the home of Democratic U. Ilhan Omar, a startling escalation in a criminal investigation that brings renewed scrutiny to th...
articles.body:
Federal agents on Monday searched the home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, a startling escalation in a criminal investigation that brings renewed scrutiny to the frequent target of Trump administration derision in the final weeks of her reelection bid .

The Justice Department confirmed that a judicially authorized search warrant of Omar's home was executed by Homeland Security Investigations but provided no other details. Trump administration officials have repeatedly hinted at the existence of an inquiry targeting the Minnesota representative. Omar called the search an "attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."

A senior U.S. official said President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are considering firing U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after a series of reports alleging she has engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.

And a bipartisan group of senators is calling on the Trump administration to "immediately reverse course" on a plan to purchase diesel from Russia despite a U.S. sanctions law.

Sen. Jon Husted tries to rally Trump crowd against Democratic opponent

The Ohio Republican is facing a stiff challenge from former Sen. Sherrod Brown. Husted, who was appointed in 2024 to replace JD Vance when he ran for vice president, sounded more like a challenger as he raked Brown for the Democrat's decades in office.

"He's been in office for over 50 years. Can you name one thing he's done to make your life better?" Husted asked the Youngstown crowd.

Brown first entered office in 1975 as a member of Ohio's statehouse.

Trump is scheduled to speak in Youngstown to boost Husted's campaign. The Republican senator's struggles in a state the president easily won in all three of his campaigns shows the challenges facing the GOP this election.

Omar supporters turn out for her at Minnesota rally

More than 100 people chanted "Ilhan! Ilhan!" at an afternoon rally in Minneapolis in support of Omar. Speakers addressed the crowd from the bed of a pickup truck behind a large sign that said, "We Stand With Ilhan."

"This administration is a violent authoritative regime. Take it from us: We would know. We have been experiencing this for generations," said Rachel Dionne-Thunder, a member of the Big Stone Cree Nation.

State Sen. Zaynab Mohamed, who was born in Somalia, said the search was a "disgusting attack" and should worry everyone.

"They're attacking her because she represents what every Somali American can be: a young Somali woman, a young hijabi mom, who can be in Congress, who can be herself, who stands up for her community without fear," Mohamed said.

Trump goes to Ohio with 2 guests: ex-NFL coach Jon Gruden and influencer Jake Paul

The president boarded Air Force One with a pair of Ohio-born celebrities ahead of a rally in Youngstown.

Trump exited Marine One with the former NFL coach and the social media influencer turned boxer.

Gruden was born in Sandusky, Ohio, and won the Super Bowl in 2003 as the head coach of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He previously spoke at Trump's recent rally in Vandalia, Ohio, near Dayton.

Paul was born in Cleveland, found fame on YouTube and became a boxer who fought the former heavyweight champion Mike Tyson.

Trump says he may meet with North Korea's leader during a trip to Asia next month

The president, who is going to China next month to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, told reporters that he may meet with Kim Jong Un while he's in Asia.

Trump said earlier this year that he planned to meet with Kim sometime this year.

Trump says he's 'not happy' with Guilfoyle after reports alleging questionable behavior by the ambassador

Asked if he was considering firing Kimberly Guilfoyle from her post as the U.S. ambassador to Greece, Trump told reporters: "Well, we're looking at it. We're not happy."

A series of recent news reports have alleged that Guilfoyle — who at one point was engaged to Trump's son Donald Trump Jr. — has engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens, including offering to use her influence inside the administration in return for the payment of a large credit card bill.

Trump says he's spoken to the Saudi crown prince after attack in Riyadh

The president confirmed to reporters that he spoke to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, but he didn't offer any details about the call. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen for the attack.

Trump, in response to another question about the Houthis, said "they are misbehaving very badly. No good." But he didn't say anything about whether the U.S. would respond to the Houthis.

Trump says there's an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia because he said so

Trump is insisting that an energy ceasefire is in place for Ukraine and Russia, despite Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying that Moscow struck his country's energy sites.

"Well, they agreed," Trump told reporters. "Because I said, 'You agree.' That's why they agreed, because I said they agree."

When pressed about the attacks by Russia, Trump said: "Well, I'd have to look at it and see, because there's been violations on both sides."

Trump says he has 'nothing to do' with search of Omar's Washington home

"I understand they're looking at it very carefully," the president said of an investigation that sparked federal agents to search the home of the Democratic representative.

Trump said he'd found the congresswoman to "be totally crooked, personally."

"But that has nothing to do with me. I think she's a terrible person, just a complainer. She comes from a country that's a non-country," Trump continued. "And then she comes over here and she complains about our Constitution."

He added, "I think she's a terrible person. But that's really up to the DOJ. I have nothing to do with it."

Trump administration says it didn't have time to cancel ads that aired after a judge's deadline

A federal judge on Sunday ordered the Trump administration to cancel any remaining TV commercials in its pro-Trump ad campaign that has cost taxpayers millions.

But even after the judge's 6:45 p.m. deadline , a few of the spots labeled as paid for by the U.S. government aired on television, data from AdImpact shows.

The Department of Homeland Security did not receive notice from the court in time to cancel those final ad buys, the White House said in an email.

The White House said the ads, which it refers to as public service announcements, will be paid for by outside groups going forward.

Trump says he'll have a rally in Kansas to boost Sen. Roger Marshall

The president said he'll have a "Kansas Style Rally, in Roger's Honor, very soon," in a lengthy social media post Monday attacking Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton's leadership at the nation's largest United Methodist church.

Marshall's race is considered a tossup, even though Democrats haven't won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932.

Hamilton founded the Kansas City-area Church of the Resurrection in 1990, which has grown to 25,000 members. That's been among his key selling points as a candidate.

When Trump previously denounced Hamilton as a "lunatic," Hamilton told a crowd in Topeka, "That is so cool! I love this!"

Iowa GOP Senate candidate says Russia should still face sanctions

Rep. Ashley Hinson said "it makes me a little bit nervous anytime we're talking about relieving a sanction on Russia."

Hinson is the Republican facing a competitive race for U.S. Senate in Iowa, where $6 diesel prices have become an issue in the campaign against Democrat Josh Turek.

Trump said last week he struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, reversing years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine.

After touring an ethanol plant in Dyersville, Iowa, Hinson told reporters that fuel prices are a priority for her. But she also said the U.S. should be "strong" on Russia, noting her support for a sanctions package that the House passed last month.

Top of the ticket in Georgia will share the stage with Trump

Georgia GOP gubernatorial nominee Rick Jackson hasn't rushed to share stages with Republican Senate nominee Mike Collins.

But Trump's trip Friday to Dalton, in north Georgia, will get the two nominees in front of the same audience, their spokesmen confirmed.

Jackson, a self-funding billionaire, is viewed as being in a considerably stronger position against Democratic nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms than Collins is in his challenge of Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff.

Strategists from both parties say Georgia could see a split result this fall.

Despite their different courses, Collins and Jackson both have Trump's endorsement — at least now. Trump endorsed Collins ahead of the GOP runoff.

Trump had endorsed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in 2025 and offered his support only after Jackson defeated Jones in a runoff.

Mailers pushing socialist candidate over Sherrod Brown linked to MAGA-tied vendor

Campaign mailers urging Ohio voters to support a socialist U.S. Senate candidate over Democratic nominee Sherrod Brown are being underwritten by a newly incorporated PAC with ties to businesses associated with Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC.

The mailers sponsored by Enough Promises Ohio PAC began arriving in voter mailboxes in recent days.

They promote independent Greg Levy over Brown with messages such as "Join the Revolution" and "Send a Worker to the Senate."

Levy has condemned the mailers as misleading "dirty tricks."

Brown is locked in a tight race against Republican Sen. Jon Husted.

Collins announces Bath shipyard clears hurdle to order destroyer

Bath Iron Works, a subsidiary of General Dynamics, is a shipyard in Maine Republican Sen. Susan Collins' home state.

It was certified Monday by the Pentagon as having made operational and managerial improvements to allow the department to order a guided-missile Navy destroyer. It would be the second to be built in fiscal year 2027.

Collins is chair of the appropriations committee and is in a competitive campaign for a sixth term against Democrat Troy Jackson.

During debates with Jackson last week, Collins argued that she uses her leadership on the key committee to benefit the Maine economy, while Jackson has criticized her for supporting the Trump administration's agenda.

Committee staff say the Bath project has a budget of $2 billion to $2.5 billion and is estimated to include roughly 6,800 jobs.

Congressional Black Caucus condemns 'politically motivated' search of Omar's home

In a statement, Chair Yvette Clarke blamed the search on Trump's "fixation" on Omar, a vocal critic of the president and his policies. Omar is a member of the caucus.

"The sustained campaign of attacks against Congresswoman Omar by the President and his allies should raise grave concerns about the politicization of federal law enforcement and the use of government power to intimidate political opponents," the statement read.

"Over the past year alone, (Trump) has repeatedly targeted Somali Americans and the state of Minnesota with vile, racist rhetoric while deploying thousands of armed ICE agents to the Twin Cities in operations targeting Somali American communities, resulting in the deaths of two Americans in broad daylight."

Judge orders Trump administration to halt work for a day on DC golf course

A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to halt work for a day on a historic D.C. golf course, pending more court action. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued the order Monday after a tense three-hour hearing in which she blistered the government for having deceived her with its actions over the holiday weekend.

Republicans react to Omar by using her own words

Responding to Omar's social media reaction addressing the search, the Republican National Committee posted a screen grab of an X post from Omar in which she wrote, "No one is above the law."

The screen grab wasn't dated, but Omar posted that phrase on social media as the House debated Trump's first impeachment case in 2019.

The Republican Party in Omar's home state of Minnesota circulated remarks it attributed to Omar from 2023, when she reacted to Trump's indictment on charges in New York by calling for people to "support accountability and to follow the facts where they lead."

Democrats condemn Omar search as political targeting ahead of election

Across social media, congressional Democrats criticized Trump for the search of Omar's home.

Calling it "unprecedented, but unfortunately not surprising," Michigan Rep. Debbie Dingell wrote that Trump had "repeatedly targeted Congresswoman Omar with hateful rhetoric, contributing to death threats and violence."

Arizona Rep. Adellita Grijalva said it represented "the latest — and darkest — chapter of Trump's racist political persecution against Ilhan Omar and the entire Somali-American community."

Saying Trump was "weaponizing our government against his perceived political opponents," Colorado Rep. Jason Crow referenced the administration's unsuccessful attempt to indict him and other congressional Democrats for a video calling on service members to defy "illegal orders."

Kremlin relishes in the US-Russia diesel deal

The deal between Moscow and Washington on exports of Russian diesel and fresh U.S. criticism of Ukraine's leader mark important political victories for the Kremlin.

While the size of Russia's diesel exports is relatively small and unlikely to significantly impact prices, the revenue will help Moscow replenish its war coffers.

More importantly, it will undermine efforts by Kyiv and its European allies to put up a united front to Putin.

Remarks by Trump suggesting that Ukraine should get a new leader also strengthen the Kremlin's hand.

Khanna calls search of Omar's home 'chilling'

Fellow progressive Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna of California also called it "disturbing" that the Trump administration is "targeting Muslim Americans and a Muslim American woman legislator." Khanna made the remarks in a video posted on social media.

Khanna added that "any decent American needs to stand up and speak out."

Fellow members of The Squad express support for Omar

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York called the search of Omar's home "an unprecedented abuse of power," saying Trump's administration had long "launched slanderous attacks" against the Minnesota Democrat.

Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib said the search is "exactly what a fascist police state does."

Omar, Tlaib and Ocasio-Cortez are part of The Squad , a group of progressive lawmakers who have endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term.

Both Tlaib and Ocasio-Cortez off on their social media posts by saying, "I stand with Ilhan."

Archbishop says Catholic soldiers should not serve on firing squad

Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who oversees the Catholic Church's pastoral services to Catholics in the U.S. military, is condemning the proposed livestream of the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan.

Broglio also is stipulating that any Catholic soldier assigned to the firing squad should ask to be excused from that duty, which he described as contrary to the teachings of the church. He joins other Catholic leaders in speaking out against the death penalty and the livestream plans.

Hasan, an Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people in 2009 at Fort Hood in Texas, is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3.

"The US military generally enjoys a good reputation in the world," Broglio said. "Is there really a value to throwing them in the same boat with terrorists by broadcasting the image of the execution of a man in a wheelchair to the whole world?"

Omar's spokesperson calls search 'outrageous' and 'unprecedented'

"This raid by Trump's DHS is an outrageous abuse of power and an unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies," Jacklyn Rogers, Omar's spokesperson, said in a statement. "For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back. Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies."

Omar calls search the 'latest escalation' in Trump's 'intimidation' campaign

"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," she said. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."

Trump said at campaign rally that 'our people' were investigating Omar

Trump and fellow Republicans from the highest ranks of party leadership have repeatedly and publicly criticized the Somali-born Omar over her status as an immigrant and her progressive views . Trump as recently as this past weekend brought up Omar at a rally in Tennessee, where he attacked her upbringing and suggested that Vice President JD Vance "and our people" were investigating her.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said last month that there was an "ongoing investigation" related in part to whether Omar lied on her immigration forms and that "something's going to happen."

House Democratic leaders condemn the search of congresswoman's home as an 'abuse of power'

"For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations," House Democratic leaders said in a statement. "Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family."

The search of the Minnesota congresswoman 's home so close to next month's midterm contests that will determine control of the House and Senate was swiftly condemned by top Democrats in Congress and raised questions about the timing given longstanding Justice Department protocol to avoid overt investigative steps involving political candidates in the direct run-up to an election.

Paid advertisements for 'Musk' are being rejected by social media companies

As of Sept. 25, YouTube, Meta, TikTok and X had all refused advertisements for the film paid by its distributor, Bleecker Street. YouTube and Meta later reversed course, saying the trailer had been flagged for "political content."

There are also concerns about whether "Musk" will eventually land on HBO as originally planned, in the aftermath of the Skydance merger created by Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. CEO David Ellison's father, Larry Ellison, is friendly with Musk.

"Would Musk be able to call Larry or David and say, you know, don't put this doc on? Yeah," Gibney said in an interview with the AP.

Gibney wrote on X that his film is "about a 'free-speech absolutist' who has threatened a lawsuit to try to stop the film from being seen."
